plan.contextChunk: This figure shows one undirected weighted graph in which a spanning tree has been picked out by shading. Nine circular vertices carry italic letters: b, c, and d sit across the top, e at the right, f at the lower right, g along the bottom, h at the lower left, a at the left, and i in the middle. Fourteen straight edges join them, each annotated with an integer weight: a-b is 4, b-c is 8, c-d is 7, d-e is 9, a-h is 8, b-h is 11, h-i is 7, h-g is 1, g-i is 6, i-c is 2, c-f is 4, g-f is 2, d-f is 14, and e-f is 10. Eight of those edges, namely a-b, b-c, c-d, d-e, c-i, c-f, h-g, and g-f, are drawn with a broad gray band running behind the line, while the other six remain thin black strokes. The shading is what the reader compares against: it marks an acyclic subset that still reaches every vertex, so the weights along it can be summed and weighed against the heavier unshaded edges it leaves out. The drawing supplies a concrete instance of the wiring problem, in which pins are vertices, possible interconnections are edges, and an edge weight is the amount of wire needed to make that connection.

interactionPlan.concept: A minimum spanning tree connects every vertex of a weighted undirected graph with an acyclic set of edges of minimum total weight — and it need not be unique, since swapping equal-weight boundary edges can yield another tree with the same total.
elements: nine circular vertices labeled a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i in italic letters
vertex positions: b, c, d across the top; a at left; i in the middle; h lower left; g bottom center; f lower right; e at right
14 undirected edges with integer weight labels: a-b (4), b-c (8), c-d (7), d-e (9), a-h (8), b-h (11), h-i (7), h-g (1), g-i (6), i-c (2), c-f (4), g-f (2), d-f (14), e-f (10)
broad gray band behind the eight tree edges: a-b, b-c, c-d, d-e, c-i, c-f, h-g, g-f
six non-tree edges drawn as thin black strokes: a-h, b-h, h-i, g-i, d-f, e-f
running total-weight readout for the shaded tree
edge info annotation showing the selected edge's weight and in/out-of-tree status
vertex reached/unreached marking during the step-through

interactions.teaches: Each edge has a weight and a role — either it belongs to the shaded spanning tree or it is excluded — and selecting it reveals why: including a heavier excluded edge would either create a cycle or force out a lighter edge, raising the total

interactions.label: Spanning tree
interactions.teaches: Swapping the equal-weight edge b-c for a-h moves the gray band but leaves the total at 37, so a minimum spanning tree is not necessarily unique

interactions.label: Build tree edge by edge
interactions.teaches: Adding the eight tree edges one at a time shows the running weight climbing to 37 and the reached-vertex set growing until every vertex is spanned without ever closing a cycle

demo_steps.title: The wiring problem
demo_steps.narration: Nine pins (vertices) must be wired together; each edge is a possible connection whose weight is the wire it costs. The gray band marks one cheapest way to connect all nine — a minimum spanning tree of total weight 37.

demo_steps.title: Build the tree edge by edge
demo_steps.narration: Step through the eight tree edges: each press adds one gray edge, updates the running total, and marks newly reached vertices. Nine vertices, exactly eight edges, no cycle — that is what makes it a spanning tree.

demo_steps.title: Inspect an excluded edge
demo_steps.narration: Click any thin edge, like b-h (11) or d-f (14): it was left out because the tree already connects its endpoints more cheaply — adding it would create a cycle whose other edges are all lighter.

demo_steps.title: Another minimum tree
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to the alternate tree: b-c (8) drops out and a-h (8) takes its place. The gray band moves, but the total stays 37 — a minimum spanning tree need not be unique.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A spanning tree on n vertices always has exactly n−1 edges and no cycles; the minimum one minimizes total weight, and equal-weight edges can make several different trees tie for minimum.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Match the textbook layout of CLRS Figure 23.1: b, c, d spaced across the top row; a mid-left; i centered slightly left of middle; h lower-left; g bottom-center; f lower-right; e mid-right. Vertices are light gray filled circles with thin black outlines and italic serif letter labels. Edge weights are plain serif numerals placed near each edge's midpoint, offset to avoid overlap (11 sits left of the vertical b-h edge, 14 left of d-f, 2 beside i-c, 4 beside c-f). Tree edges carry a broad translucent gray band behind the black line; non-tree edges are thin black lines only. In the alternate-tree toggle, the band on b-c moves to a-h (and vertex connectivity should remain visibly spanning). During the step-through, unreached vertices can be dimmed and the running total shown in a corner readout.

authoredContext: We can model this wiring problem with a connected, undirected graph G D .V; E/, where V is the set of pins, E is the set of possible interconnections between pairs of pins, and for each edge .u; _x0017_/ 2 E, we have a weight w.u; _x0017_/ specifying the cost (amount of wire needed) to connect u and _x0017_. We then wish to find an acyclic subset T _x0012_ E that connects all of the vertices and whose total weight w.T / D X .u;_x0017_/2T w.u; _x0017_/ is minimized. Since T is acyclic and connects all of the vertices, it must form a tree, which we call a spanning tree since it “spans” the graph G. We call the problem of determining the tree T the minimum-spanning-tree problem. 1 Figure 23.1 shows an example of a connected graph and a minimum spanning tree.

action_items: Fix the load-time crash: rename the global 'var V' vertex map (e.g. to 'POS') — the top-level name V collides with a symbol the scaffold/library expects to be callable, producing 'V is not a function' before anything draws.

After fixing, verify the gray bands render behind the black edges (bandGroup.back() is called before edges exist in z-order terms — ensure bands sit below edges but above the background) and that all 14 weight labels and 9 vertex labels match the source layout.
Re-test all controls post-fix (step player, Build-tree button, tree-choice checkbox, edge click popups) since none could be validated in the crashed state.
